intro_html: Employee Resignation & Clearance turns a resignation into a record that carries itself to the end — the last working day worked out from the employee's own notice period, an approval trail behind every stage, a clearance checklist routed to the people who own each item, and a release that refuses outright while company property is still in their hands.

features.title: The Release Refuses, Live
features.desc: The property register is re-read at the moment somebody presses Release. If anything is still out, the refusal names the item, its handover reference and the date it was due back.

features.title: Last Working Day, Worked Out
features.desc: Read from the employee's own notice period the moment notice is given — and left alone for good the instant a person types a negotiated date over it.

features.title: A Checklist With Owners
features.desc: One line per clearance item, each routed to the person who owns it with a to-do in their inbox, and a progress figure above the list.

features.title: Approval, Stage By Stage
features.desc: Notice, the manager's sign-off, HR approval, clearance, release. Whether the manager step runs at all is one switch per company.

features.title: The Manager Sees One Record
features.desc: There is no menu for resignations outside HR. The leaver's own manager reaches exactly the record they must approve, and every other ordinary user reaches none.

features.title: Released On The Day, By Itself
features.desc: A daily run releases what is due and fully cleared, using the same two checks as the button — no shortcut, no elevated bypass.

features.title: Final Once Released
features.desc: Dates, reason and checklist lock in the code itself, not merely on the screen: a script or an API call is refused exactly like the form is.

features.title: Exit Interview, Tracked
features.desc: Send the survey from the record and see whether it went out and whether it came back, with the answer one click away.

limitations: When company property is still outstanding, the checklist shows Company Property twice — once as the ordinary pending line and once as a blocked line naming what is out, its handover reference and its due date. Both have to be cleared. With nothing outstanding the checklist is exactly the items you configured.
There is no way back to the calculated date. Once a last working day is typed in by hand it stays that way; putting it back to the proposed date needs a developer.

The property register is read, never written. Releasing somebody does not mark their items returned — that has to happen in the custody register first, or the release stays blocked. That is deliberate.
Archiving the login is skipped in two cases: when it is the system account, or when it is the very person pressing Release. Odoo forbids both writes; everything else in the release still completes.
No contract end date without a contract start date. Where the employee's current record has no start date, that one write is skipped and a note is posted on the record instead.

The Ukrainian pack covers every label, state, button and message the module raises. The five starter checklist item names are ordinary records, so their Ukrainian wording is a reference translation rather than a live one — renaming them is an administrator's job.
Out of scope entirely: no final settlement and no payslip, no dismissal workflow, no handover tasks, no exit-interview reporting, no self-service resignation and no generated documents.
